name: DB-Editable Ask Responses
description: i need you make sure all the ai like responses can be edited via db as the backend is at /home/quantumbytes/Documents/Q_PROJECTS/kaascan_bkd/endpoints/ask.py go then make sure if we need we can edit the response in the database

goal.answer: Make the AI-like response strings in the ask.py endpoint configurable via the SystemSetting database table, so they can be edited through the existing /admin/settings/update API without changing the response shape.

criteria.answer:
ask.py reads response strings from SystemSetting table instead of hardcoded strings
All response fields (response, message, action_message, status: 'error' response) are configurable via unique keys
Fallback to current hardcoded string when a SystemSetting key is absent
Existing response JSON structure (status, type, response, message, students, etc.) is unchanged
A new ask response payload (e.g. /ask/responses endpoint or GET-based read) is NOT required — the existing /admin/settings/update endpoint is sufficient for editing

constraints.answer: No changes to the response JSON shape — Flutter ChatBubble must continue to parse it identically, Use the existing SystemSetting model (already in core/models.py), not a new table, Must work via the existing get_db() session — no new DB connection pattern, Keep the ask.py endpoint as a single @router.post('/ask') — don't split into multiple endpoints

phases.answer: Phase 1 — Refactor ask.py to source responses from SystemSetting

phases.name: Phase 1 — Refactor ask.py to source responses from SystemSetting
phases.goal: Modify ask.py to read all response/message/action_message strings from SystemSetting DB table, with hardcoded fallback defaults.

steps.description: Define a helper function or dict mapping to load each response string key from SystemSetting, e.g. ask_no_query_response, ask_not_found_response, ask_found_response, ask_found_message, ask_multiple_response, ask_multiple_message, ask_multiple_action_message. Include a fallback map of current hardcoded strings as defaults.
Replace each hardcoded string in ask.py with a lookup call (e.g. load_setting('ask_no_query_response')) so the strings come from DB.
Verify the endpoint still works: run the FastAPI app and POST to /ask with a test query, confirm response shape is identical.
